cfo_brief: Revenue fell $3.87B (-15.4%) sequentially, from $25.17B in Q4 2023 to $21.30B in Q1 2024, as confirmed in filings dated January 24 and April 23, 2024, respectively. A same-day Reuters report accompanying the 10-Q attributes the drop to aggressive ASP price cuts made to stimulate demand, framing this explicitly as a margin-compression story rather than a unit-volume collapse. The decline likely reflects a compounding effect of normal seasonal softness following the historically strong Q4 delivery push, layered with structural pricing erosion from the deliberate strategy to prioritize volume over per-unit revenue.

external_signal.headline: Price cuts pressure auto margin as TSLA attempts to spur demand.
